title: GeoToSchemtic
description: Convert KML and GeoJSON files to Minecraft schematics for BuildTheEarth project!
description2:
Upload your files and set the desired settings, then click "Convert".
Use //paste -o -a command to paste your converted schematic into the correct position in BTE projection.
status_success: Success! Use "//paste -a -o" to correctly place your schematic
status_error: Error while reading the file. Please make sure that your file is valid and contains geodata
status_error_loadconverter: Failed to load converter, check your connection to GitHub
status_error_whileprocessing: Unknown error while processing data from your file =(
status_error_toobig: Hold on, your file is too big for one schematic! How about splitting it into smaller ones?
status_error_wronglegacyid: Wrong block ID, please use text IDs of blocks that are presented in 1.12.2
status_error_exceedminecraftlimit: The size of the proposed schematic exceeds the limits set by Minecraft
status_error_wrongcoordsformat: Your file contains coordinates in an unsupported format. The coordinates of each point must be expressed as latitude and longitude (and, optionally, altitude) as decimal degrees
originexplanation: Coordinates for Litematica. For WorldEdit, use only //paste with the -o flag!
offset_tooltip:
Additional schematic offset.
Some BTE servers have an additional world offset, for example to fit mountains within the vanilla height limit. Enter this offset here, and it will be added to the schematic's original BTE-projection coordinates. Most servers don't have world offset; check is your server is listed in the "Offset presets".
conselevation_tooltip: Place objects at their expected height in the schematic based on their elevation value specified in the source file. Objects without an elevation will be placed at Y level 0.<hr>If unchecked, all objects will be on Y level 0. You can move them to another level using Y offset.
fillterrain_tooltip:
Fill the spaces between contour lines at the desired heights, recreating the intended relief. For topographic maps only!
Emerald blocks will be generated between all diamond blocks along the X and Z axes. There must be a vertical interval of 0-1 meter between contours, and they must not intersect. Failure to meet these conditions will break the infill. Also, for curved contours, the infill may be generated 1 block higher than intended, but this is easy to notice and correct manually.
makefoundation_tooltip: Creates a foundation under all blocks in the schematic. This brings convenience to terraforming, particularly when working with falling blocks.
interpolatecontours_tooltip: Experimental feature for generating new contours between existing contours with large vertical spacing (2 or more blocks). Enable this only if you know what you're doing!
privacynotice:
Privacy notice: all files are processed by your local machine
and aren't uploaded to any server.
alert_error_wrongid: Please enter a valid Minecraft block ID. Only text IDs are supported
alert_error_offset: Please enter correct offset values. Offset values can only be integers
alert_toomuchvolume:
The proposed schematic has a very large volume of blocks. Please note that pasting such a schematic may be prohibited on servers without the administration's consent.
Click "OK" to continue the conversion; "Cancel" to cancel the conversion.
